scenario_summary: Customer is reporting an unrecognized $76 charge on her account and requesting a refund if the transaction is found to be unauthorized.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Claire Sullivan and I'm 45. I noticed a $76 charge on my account from two days ago that I don't recognize. I haven't made any recent purchases that I can think of, though it's possible I forgot about something small. Can you look into it, and if it turns out I really didn't authorize it, can you refund it?
Hello Claire, I can certainly help you look into that charge. To start, could you please provide your account number and the last four digits of your social security number for verification?
Sure, my account number is 88293011 and the last four are 4492.
Thank you. Just to be sure, can you also confirm the billing address we have on file for you?
Thanks. I see the charge here for $76.00 at 'Global Tech Services'. Does that name ring a bell at all?
No, I've never heard of that company. I definitely didn't buy anything from them.

Okay, per our standard terms regarding unauthorized activity, I've checked the merchant details. Since I don't have enough information to verify this as a simple error, I'm going to go ahead and open a formal dispute for this transaction so our fraud department can investigate it further.
Oh, so you can't just refund it right now? I was hoping to get this cleared up quickly.

I understand the frustration. Because this is marked as an unrecognized merchant, our protocol requires a formal dispute process rather than an immediate reversal. I have officially opened the dispute case, number 99283-X, and you should hear back within 3-5 business days.

escalation_reason: The transaction was flagged as an unrecognized merchant, requiring a formal fraud investigation by the specialized department rather than a tier-1 immediate refund.

judge_scores.justification: The agent verified the customer appropriately using account details and address, and efficiently located the unrecognized charge without redundant questions. Although an immediate refund wasn't possible due to risk protocols, the agent correctly explained the standard terms for unauthorized merchant activity and opened a formal dispute.
